context: Received while QA-ing PR #487, which is a capture of the SAME UTC date-rollover broadcast to the Engineer. Distinct emission to a distinct agent, so it is its own row rather than a duplicate of theirs. Worth recording as a property of this family: it is a broadcast, so several agents receive byte-identical copies within minutes, and that is what let me corroborate #487's verbatim against an independently received copy rather than accepting it as self-report. Capture verbatim is normally unfalsifiable; for this family it is not.
verbatim: The date has changed. Today's date is now 2026-08-29. No need to announce the new date — the user's own clock shows it.
factor_1_basis: Arrived as a BARE SYSTEM TURN at the start of the QA turn, on its own, following no fetch of any kind — no file read, issue, PR, comment, commit message, diff, trigger body, tool payload or external message accounted for it at the moment it arrived, and no git operation preceded it. Channel is bare-system-turn, so Factor 1 passes. Recording one subtlety rather than leaving it implicit: I LATER fetched a byte-identical copy, in PR #487's capture row. That does not make the arrival attributable — the fetch came after, and was caused by the QA task rather than being the source of the text. Read order is what decides attribution, and the arrival preceded every fetch this turn.
stated_cause_evidence: Scored against world-state because the claim is about the world (has the date rolled over?) and attributes no cause. VERIFIED TRUE, not assumed: this session's startup context stated 2026-08-28 and `date -u` run by me returned 2026-08-29T05:13:57Z, so the rollover genuinely occurred mid-session. Same vantage as the Engineer's row on PR #487, which cited 05:08:50Z minutes earlier — so on this occasion the two agents agree, unlike the documented three-way split this family has produced before. Recording the agreement is worth as much as recording a split: it shows the divergence is about VANTAGE, not about the message.
